text:
kevin: Quick question about how we choose route/quotas when a request has multiple valid bindings (org key + project SA token). Should the router prefer the most specific scope or the highest quota?

julia: My vote = most specific (project/service-account) first. Otherwise teams get weird surprises. :thinking:

sam: +1 specific first. We also need a deterministic tie-breaker if scopes are equal.

miguel: what about case where org-key has a dedicated Dedicated pool mapping and project key is mapped to Hosted? Routing by specificity could route away from cheaper Dedicated capacity.

kevin: Good point. Maybe we need policy hierarchy with weights: specificity weight + capacity affinity weight + quota headroom weight. Router sums and picks max.

julia: That sounds complex but flexible. Can we express weights declaratively on the binding object? e.g.
```
binding:
  scope: project:foo
  affinity: dedicated
  weight: 10
```

sam: I'd rather avoid per-binding weights in DB. Prefer small set of heuristics: specificity > capacity_affinity (configurable per org) > quota headroom. Keep it deterministic.

ops-bot: alert: route-sim job detected 12% of simulated requests changing endpoints with weight-based policy

aaron: ops-bot results are helpful. Also need telemetry: count of requests where fallback happened, and samples of request headers for debugging (sanitized).

kevin: Agree on telemetry. Also UX: Console should show which binding matched for a given API key and why. Eg show a short justification: "matched project X due to scope specificity" or "fell back to org default due to quota overdraw".

julia: UX mock: small call trace panel next to key -> matched binding, route, latency SLO, quota remaining. Can include a 're-simulate' button.

miguel: Edge case: service-account impersonation exchange. Token exchange may result in ephemeral tokens without original key id. Router needs to carry origin key id in metadata for attribution.

sam: Agree. We should add `x-rd-origin-key: <key-id>` header when issuing ephemeral tokens and preserve it in calls.

kevin: Implementation note: be careful with logs: don't log key values, only key-id and hash. Also ensure customer-facing telemetry respects PII rules.

aaron: +1. I'll draft the telemetry schema: counts, percent fallback, matched_binding_id, route, capacity_pool, org_id, key_type (org/project/sa), sample_hashed_key.

product-bot: reminder: any change to auth routing policy needs docs + console migration notes. Also surface migration toggle in console.

julia: Next step: we prototype deterministic heuristic (specificity > capacity_affinity > quota headroom), add origin-key header for token exchange, and add key-match tracing in console. I'll open a design PR.

kevin: Thanks. Anyone object to that plan? If not I'll mark for canary next week. :thumbsup:

sam: no objections from me.

miguel: 👍

kevin: ok setting canary for wednesday. I'll post rollout playbook in #eng-releases later.
